unpatched_known_rce_cve.title: Unpatched Known Pre-Auth RCE CVE
unpatched_known_rce_cve.description: Interpreted boolean (assessor-derived): TRUE when the NGFW appliance firmware is at or below a release affected by a publicly-known, CISA-KEV-listed pre-auth RCE/auth-bypass CVE (e.g. PAN-OS GlobalProtect CVE-2024-3400; FortiOS SSL-VPN CVE-2024-21762) and is NOT at/above the vendor's fixed release. Polarity-safe positive-insecure: the patched appliance is FALSE so the all-secure baseline stays silent.

vpn_portal_service_internet_exposed.title: VPN/Portal Service Internet-Exposed
vpn_portal_service_internet_exposed.description: Interpreted boolean: TRUE when the appliance's internet-facing services carrying the pre-auth surface — GlobalProtect gateway/portal (PAN-OS) or SSL-VPN/sslvpnd (FortiOS) — are reachable from untrusted/internet zones. Necessary second AND condition for the pre-auth RCE to be remotely exploitable. Secure posture (not internet-reachable / behind a VPN-broker) is FALSE.

edge_appliance_patched_within_sla.title: Edge Appliance Patched Within SLA
edge_appliance_patched_within_sla.description: Shared workspace vocabulary: TRUE when the edge appliance firmware (FortiOS/FortiProxy/PAN-OS) is patched to the fixed release within the remediation SLA (e.g. CISA BOD 22-01 KEV deadlines). Read with is_false: the exposure fires when the appliance is NOT patched within SLA. This is the patch-currency expression of the firmware hazard and the management-plane auth-bypass precondition (CVE-2022-40684 present only on unpatched firmware).

admin_interface_internet_reachable.title: Admin Interface Internet-Reachable
admin_interface_internet_reachable.description: TRUE when the firewall's administrative/management interface (FortiGate allowaccess https/ssh on an external interface, or PAN-OS mgmt profile without a restrictive permitted-IP list) is reachable from untrusted/internet source ranges rather than restricted to dedicated management subnets. The precondition that turns a management-plane auth-bypass flaw (e.g. CVE-2022-40684) into a remotely exploitable admin takeover.

control_plane_api_not_publicly_exposed.title: Control-Plane API Not Publicly Exposed
control_plane_api_not_publicly_exposed.description: Shared-workspace attestation: TRUE when the device's control-plane/management API (the HTTP/HTTPS admin endpoint a bypass request targets) is NOT exposed to public/untrusted networks. Secure value is TRUE; the exposure fires when FALSE (the API is publicly exposed), making a crafted-request authentication bypass reachable by an unauthenticated remote attacker.

edge_management_interfaces_not_internet_.title: Edge Management Interfaces Not Internet-Reachable
edge_management_interfaces_not_internet_.description: Shared-workspace attestation: TRUE when edge-appliance management interfaces (HTTPS/SSH/SNMP admin, GUI, CLI) are not reachable from the internet — segmented behind a management network/jump host and source-IP restricted. Secure value is TRUE; the exposure fires when FALSE, indicating the management plane is internet-reachable and exploitable by the auth bypass or default-credential attack.

default_accounts_removed_or_changed.title: Default Accounts Removed or Changed
default_accounts_removed_or_changed.description: Shared-workspace attestation: TRUE when all vendor default admin accounts/passwords (e.g. admin/admin) have been changed, renamed, or disabled so no account uses a publicly-known default credential. FALSE (vendor defaults still in use) fires this exposure via default-credential brute-force/guessing of the management plane.

mfa_available.title: MFA Available for Admin Login
mfa_available.description: Shared-workspace attestation: TRUE when multi-factor/two-factor authentication (FortiToken / RADIUS+OTP, or PAN-OS MFA-backed authentication profile) is available and enforced for privileged admin logins. FALSE (single-factor password-only) fires this exposure — no second factor to resist credential theft/guessing on the management plane.

admin_trusted_host_restriction_enabled.title: Admin Trusted-Host Restriction Enabled
admin_trusted_host_restriction_enabled.description: TRUE when every admin account/management profile restricts access to a small permitted-IP/trusted-host set (FortiGate 'config system admin' trustedhostN to specific mgmt subnets; CIS PAN-OS 1.2.1/1.2.2 Permitted IP Addresses on each SSH/HTTPS/SNMP mgmt profile). FALSE (trustedhost empty/0.0.0.0/0 or no permitted-IP list) fires this exposure — the admin plane accepts logins from any source.

rate_limiting_or_lockout_enabled.title: Rate Limiting or Account Lockout Enabled
rate_limiting_or_lockout_enabled.description: Shared-workspace attestation: TRUE when failed-login lockout/rate-limiting throttles brute-force against the management plane (FortiGate admin-lockout-threshold + admin-lockout-duration non-zero; CIS PAN-OS 1.4.2 Failed Attempts & Lockout Time non-zero). FALSE (lockout disabled / unlimited attempts) fires this exposure via unthrottled credential brute force.

http_or_telnet_admin_enabled.title: HTTP or Telnet Admin Access Enabled
http_or_telnet_admin_enabled.description: Interpreted from the management interface allowaccess / mgmt-profile (FortiOS 'config system interface set allowaccess', CIS PAN 1.2.3-1.2.4): TRUE when cleartext admin protocols HTTP or Telnet are permitted on any management interface. Secure posture allows only HTTPS + SSH, so the secure value is FALSE. TRUE exposes admin credentials and config to sniffing/MITM on the management path.

weak_tls_versions_enabled.title: Weak TLS Versions Enabled (Management)
weak_tls_versions_enabled.description: Shared workspace vocabulary. Interpreted boolean over the composite admin-https-ssl-versions directive (FortiOS 'show system global | grep admin-https-ssl-versions'): TRUE when legacy SSL/TLS 1.0/1.1 are enabled for the admin HTTPS plane. Modelled as an interpreted boolean (not a substring match) so the secure value 'tlsv1-2'/'tlsv1-3' does not false-fire. Secure value is FALSE (TLS 1.2 minimum).

min_tls_version.title: Minimum TLS Version (Management)
min_tls_version.description: Shared workspace vocabulary — name matched to the gateway/dataFlow min_tls_version, not a local synonym. Lowest TLS protocol version accepted on the management HTTPS plane (admin-https-ssl-versions floor). Fires on the insecure values TLSv1.0/TLSv1.1; the secure floor TLSv1.2 (or TLSv1.3) does not fire.

self_signed_admin_cert.title: Self-Signed Admin Certificate
self_signed_admin_cert.description: Interpreted from admin-server-cert / browser admin certificate (CIS PAN 1.2.5): TRUE when the management GUI presents a default self-signed (or expired) certificate rather than a valid CA-issued cert. Secure value is FALSE (valid certificate from a trusted source). TRUE prevents admins from detecting MITM on the management session.

server_certificate_validated.title: Server Certificate Validated
server_certificate_validated.description: Shared workspace vocabulary. Whether the management TLS server certificate is validated against a trusted source (current validity dates, trusted issuer). Secure value is TRUE; the exposure fires when validation is absent (is_false), leaving the management session open to certificate substitution/MITM.

snmp_v1_v2c_enabled.title: SNMP v1/v2c Enabled
snmp_v1_v2c_enabled.description: Interpreted from the SNMP polling configuration (CIS PAN 1.5.1): TRUE when community-based SNMP v1/v2c is enabled. Community strings traverse the management/monitoring plane in cleartext, exposing them to sniffing. Secure posture is SNMPv3-only (authenticated + encrypted), so the secure value is FALSE.

ingress_default_deny_enforced.title: Ingress Default-Deny Enforced
ingress_default_deny_enforced.description: Shared workspace vocabulary — aligned with the ingress posture attribute used across the gateway/boundary classes. Whether the firewall policy terminates in a default-deny (drop-all) posture so traffic not matched by an explicit allow rule is blocked (NIST SP 800-41 Rev.1). TRUE = default-deny (secure); FALSE = default-permit / no terminating deny (insecure), silently allowing unintended traffic across the segmentation boundary.

implicit_deny_logged.title: Implicit Deny Logged
implicit_deny_logged.description: Whether the implicit/terminating deny rule logs the traffic it drops, producing telemetry for detection and SIEM forwarding (NIST SP 800-41 Rev.1). TRUE = implicit deny logged (secure); FALSE = deny not logged (insecure), yielding no telemetry on blocked attempts and a blind spot in segmentation enforcement.

external_siem_forwarding_enabled.title: External SIEM Forwarding Enabled
external_siem_forwarding_enabled.description: Whether the firewall forwards its logs off-box to a remote syslog/SIEM endpoint (CIS PAN 1.1.1.1 syslog profile with All Logs; CIS Controls v8 Control 8). FALSE means logs are retained only on-device, where firewall compromise or policy tampering goes undetected and on-box logs can be wiped. Fires on the insecure (no off-box forwarding) state.

denied_traffic_logging_enabled.title: Denied Traffic Logging Enabled
denied_traffic_logging_enabled.description: Whether denied/dropped traffic (including the terminating implicit-deny) is logged and exported. FALSE removes the telemetry on blocked attempts that segmentation enforcement relies on, so reconnaissance and policy-bypass attempts leave no record. Fires on the insecure (denied-traffic logging off) state.

admin_action_logging_enabled.title: Admin Action Logging Enabled
admin_action_logging_enabled.description: Whether administrative/management-plane actions (logins, privileged operations) are captured and exported to the SIEM. FALSE means admin compromise and unauthorized management-plane activity go unrecorded off-box. Fires on the insecure (admin-action logging off) state.

config_change_logging_enabled.title: Config Change Logging Enabled
config_change_logging_enabled.description: Whether firewall configuration-change events (ruleset/policy edits) are logged and exported off-box (CIS PAN System/Configuration logs). FALSE means policy tampering — silently relaxing the ruleset — produces no detectable, retained record. Fires on the insecure (config-change logging off) state.

perimeter_crossings_logged_and_centraliz.title: Perimeter Crossings Logged and Centralized
perimeter_crossings_logged_and_centraliz.description: Shared workspace vocabulary: whether traffic crossing the network perimeter the firewall enforces is logged and centralized to a common store/SIEM. FALSE means boundary crossings are not observable centrally, defeating cross-system correlation of an attack against the segmentation device. Fires on the insecure (crossings not centralized) state.

logs_stored_on_separate_system.title: Logs Stored on Separate System
logs_stored_on_separate_system.description: Shared workspace vocabulary: whether logs are stored on a system separate from the firewall that generates them, so an attacker who compromises the device cannot also delete the evidence. FALSE means on-device-only retention with no off-box copy. Fires on the insecure (logs co-located on the firewall) state.

audit_log_tamper_evident.title: Audit Log Tamper-Evident
audit_log_tamper_evident.description: Shared workspace vocabulary: whether retained audit logs are tamper-evident (write-once / integrity-protected) so on-device wiping or alteration is detectable. FALSE means logs can be silently wiped or edited after a firewall compromise. Secondary trigger; fires on the insecure (logs not tamper-evident) state.

session_table_limits_enforced.title: Session Table Limits Enforced
session_table_limits_enforced.description: Interpreted boolean: whether the firewall enforces session/connection-table protection — per-source and global session limits, SYN-flood / new-connection-rate thresholds (DoS-protection/session-rate policies) — so a flood cannot exhaust the global session table or CPU. TRUE = caps/thresholds in place; FALSE (firing/insecure) = no session-table limits, allowing connection-table exhaustion that drops legitimate traffic.

ddos_protection_in_place.title: DDoS Protection In Place
ddos_protection_in_place.description: Shared workspace vocabulary: whether anti-DDoS/flood-protection controls (rate limiting, SYN-cookie / aggregate flood thresholds, or upstream/scrubbing protection) defend the device against volumetric and protocol floods. TRUE = protection present; FALSE (firing/insecure) = the device is unprotected against floods aimed at exhausting its capacity.

fails_open_on_overload.title: Fails Open on Overload
fails_open_on_overload.description: Interpreted boolean: whether the device's behaviour under resource exhaustion/overload is fail-OPEN (passes traffic unfiltered when the session table fills or CPU saturates), silently removing the enforcement boundary. TRUE (firing/insecure) = fails open under overload; FALSE = fails closed / defined fail-safe stance that preserves enforcement.

ha_failover_configured.title: HA Failover Configured
ha_failover_configured.description: Interpreted boolean grounded in the high-availability/failover posture (CIS PAN-OS 3.1-3.3 / FortiGate HA): whether the firewall runs as an HA pair with session synchronization and link/path monitoring so a single device failure (or a flood that downs one unit) does not collapse the enforcement boundary. TRUE = HA with session sync + monitoring; FALSE (firing/insecure) = single non-HA device / no link monitoring.

ips_threat_prevention_enabled.title: IPS/Threat-Prevention Enabled
ips_threat_prevention_enabled.description: Interpreted boolean: TRUE when the NGFW's IPS/threat-prevention engine is active and inspecting traffic (PAN-OS WildFire/Threat-Prevention engine running, FortiGate IPS/AV engine enabled). FALSE means the engine is disabled and the firewall is a blind passthrough. Per CIS Palo Alto 5.3 / FortiGate IPS engine status. Exposure fires when FALSE.

threat_signatures_current.title: Threat Signatures Current
threat_signatures_current.description: Interpreted boolean: TRUE when IPS/AV/application-and-threat content signatures are current (content auto-update enabled and recently applied per CIS Palo Alto 4.1/4.2; FortiGuard content current). FALSE means signatures are stale/manual, so the engine misses known threats even when running. Exposure fires when FALSE.

security_profiles_on_allow_rules.title: Security Profiles on Allow Rules
security_profiles_on_allow_rules.description: Interpreted boolean: TRUE when every security policy with an Allow action has a threat-prevention/security profile (IPS, AV, anti-spyware, WildFire/sandboxing) attached, so permitted traffic is actually inspected. FALSE means Allow rules pass traffic without inspection — the engine may run but is not applied. Per CIS Palo Alto 5.3 / FortiGate UTM profiles on policies. Exposure fires when FALSE.

tls_inspection_enabled.title: TLS Inspection Enabled
tls_inspection_enabled.description: Interpreted boolean: TRUE when SSL/TLS decryption-and-inspection is applied to traffic crossing the boundary (where policy and privacy allow), so encrypted threats are not a blind spot. FALSE means encrypted traffic passes uninspected, letting TLS-wrapped malware/C2 and evasion cross the boundary. Secondary trigger; fires when FALSE.

config_change_detection_enabled.title: Config Change Detection Enabled
config_change_detection_enabled.description: Shared workspace vocabulary: whether changes to the firewall configuration are detected and recorded through a change-control workflow (NIST CM-3). TRUE when every config edit is captured against a tracked baseline; FALSE when rule edits are ad-hoc and unattributed, letting unauthorized rule changes silently weaken segmentation undetected.

drift_detection_enabled.title: Drift Detection Enabled
drift_detection_enabled.description: Shared workspace vocabulary: whether the running firewall config is automatically compared against a reviewed, version-controlled baseline to surface drift. TRUE when drift is detected and alerted; FALSE when no drift detection exists, leaving malicious or accidental rule changes undetectable.

running_config_matches_baseline.title: Running Config Matches Baseline
running_config_matches_baseline.description: Shared workspace vocabulary: whether the device's currently running configuration matches the approved version-controlled baseline (NIST CM-2). TRUE when running config equals the reviewed baseline; FALSE when uncontrolled drift is present, indicating the live ruleset diverges from the authorized segmentation policy.

config_backed_up_to_known_good.title: Config Backed Up to Known-Good Store
config_backed_up_to_known_good.description: Shared workspace vocabulary: whether the firewall configuration is regularly backed up off-box to a known-good, tamper-evident store. TRUE when off-box backups exist and are verified; FALSE when no off-box backup exists, making a maliciously altered config unrecoverable.

out_of_band_changes_controlled.title: Out-of-Band Changes Controlled
out_of_band_changes_controlled.description: Shared workspace vocabulary: whether out-of-band (direct CLI/GUI) edits bypassing the change-control workflow are prevented or detected via restricted change access (NIST CM-5). TRUE when OOB changes are blocked or reconciled; FALSE when admins can edit rules ad-hoc with no control, permitting silent unauthorized rule changes.
